narrative.overview:
The board is a workbook, not an app skin. It is part spreadsheet (rows, columns, cells you scan), part printed tabular paper (plain sheet, ruled lines, nothing decorative) and part CAD drawing (hairline precision, exact small type, a title block that says what the sheet is). Engineers already trust these three objects to carry a record. The board borrows their authority instead of inventing a brand world.

It is dense on purpose. The type ladder sits at 10–14px, the neutrals are zero-chroma graphite, and colour appears only when it means something: the status of a card or an agent, or the identity capsule of an agent. Dark is the default sheet (`<html class="dark">`) and light is a full peer. Every value routes through `ui/src/index.css`.

The current colour and type values are **provisional**. DESIGN-UI.md records that brand colour, type and iconography are being redesigned and will land only as token values. The neutral graphite, the primary and Inter are placeholders. The status vocabulary, the token-only structure and the workbook stance are what future work must keep.
keyCharacteristics: Achromatic graphite neutrals (OKLCH chroma 0) in both themes; colour means status.
Dense, small, exact type: Inter Variable, a named ladder at 10 / 11 / 12 / 13 / 14px.
Flat like paper. Hairline rules and tonal cell steps carry structure, not shadows.
Machine values (IDs, costs, timestamps, logs) set in the monospace stack.
Dark-default sheet with a full light theme; status hues hold up in both.
Touch floor of 44px on coarse pointers, because field engineers use it on a phone.

rules.name: The Colour Means State Rule
rules.body: On a board surface, a hue other than graphite must name a status, an agent, a match type or a destructive action. Decorative colour is not allowed.

rules.name: The One Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: A status renders through the same `--status-*` seed in a chip, a row, an icon, a chart and a log line. Never introduce a parallel status palette.

rules.name: The Title Block Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is set by weight, position and ruling, not by size. No new step above 14px enters the app chrome without a DESIGN-UI.md change.

rules.name: The Machine Type Rule
rules.body: If a machine generated the value, it is set in mono through the shared formatting helpers. It is never formatted ad hoc per screen.

rules.name: The Grid Before Whitespace Rule
rules.body: Density in service of scanning beats whitespace in service of aesthetics. Space separates groups of information; it is never added to look calm.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Anything on the sheet is flat. If an element needs to stand out, give it a rule, a tonal cell or a status seed. Do not lift it.

dos: **Do** take every colour, size, radius, shadow and motion value from `ui/src/index.css` tokens, and run `pnpm check:token-gates` before committing UI changes.
**Do** render every status through its `--status-*` seed and the `.status-chip` / `.status-fill` recipes, identically in chip, row, icon, chart and log.
**Do** set IDs, costs, token counts, timestamps and logs in the mono stack via the shared formatters.
**Do** separate surfaces with a 1px hairline rule or one tonal step.
**Do** check both themes. Dark is the default, but light is a full peer.
**Do** keep the 44px touch floor on coarse pointers for primary controls.
**Do** use the motion tokens (`--motion-duration-*`, `--motion-ease-out-expo`, `--motion-ease-standard`) and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** add hue to the neutrals or introduce decorative colour. A hue must name a state, an agent, a match type or a destructive action.
**Don't** lift in-plane elements with shadows, or extend the `--shadow-extract-*` debt.
**Don't** use hex, raw px, Tailwind bracket values or palette classes (`bg-red-500`) in `ui/src/components/**` or `ui/src/pages/**`.
**Don't** add a type size above 14px to app chrome, or a display face.
**Don't** treat the current neutrals, primary or Inter as the final brand. They are provisional until the redesign lands as token values.
**Don't** use the agent gradients for anything but the agent capsule.
